A critical section is a segment of code in which a process accesses shared resources (like variables, files, or devices). Only one process should execute in the critical section at a time to avoid race conditions .

lq.q: Explain the concept of process synchronization. Describe the working of synchronization using semaphores and explain the critical section problem along with its requirements.
answer: In a multi-process system, process synchronization ensures that concurrent processes accessing shared resources (like memory or files) do so without conflicts or inconsistencies . It prevents issues such as race conditions , deadlocks , and data corruption .

The critical section is the part of the program where a process accesses shared resources . The critical section problem is to design a protocol that ensures only one process is in its critical section at any given time.
Mutual Exclusion: No two processes should enter their critical sections at the same time.
Mutual Exclusion: No two processes should enter their critical sections at the same time.
Progress: If no process is in the critical section, others waiting should be allowed to enter without unnecessary delay.
Progress: If no process is in the critical section, others waiting should be allowed to enter without unnecessary delay.
Bounded Waiting: There should be a limit on how many times other processes can enter the critical section before a waiting process is allowed.
Bounded Waiting: There should be a limit on how many times other processes can enter the critical section before a waiting process is allowed.

#include <stdio.h> #include <pthread.h> #include <semaphore.h> sem_t mutex; void* critical_section(void* arg) { sem_wait(&mutex); // Entering critical section printf("Process %d in critical section\n", *(int*)arg); sleep(1); sem_post(&mutex); // Exiting critical section return NULL; } int main() { pthread_t t1, t2; int a = 1, b = 2; sem_init(&mutex, 0, 1); pthread_create(&t1, NULL, critical_section, &a); pthread_create(&t2, NULL, critical_section, &b); pthread_join(t1, NULL); pthread_join(t2, NULL); sem_destroy(&mutex); return 0; }
